fact: The Cyber Security Authority sanctioned bodies under Section 92 of the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), which the article treats as the law in force; the document gives no other date, so as_of is its published date.

The Cyber Security Authority fined the Office of the Registrar of Companies GH¢240,000 (10,000 penalty units for each of two instances of non-compliance, under Section 92(2) of Act 1038) and fined Purpleline Solutions Limited GH¢120,000 for providing cybersecurity services without a licence; the document gives no sanction date, so as_of is its published date.

Digital Policy Alert states that Ghana's 2020 Cybersecurity Act establishes measures for critical information infrastructure protection, cybercrime prevention and incident response, and says Ghana implemented the Act; it names the Cyber Security Authority as created under it.
The op-ed says the Cybersecurity Act of 2020 provides a framework for protecting critical information infrastructure and prosecuting cybercrimes.
MyJoyOnline names Ghana's Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038) as existing law covering impersonation, fraud and other cyber-related offences.
The article describes the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038) as the law protecting users from data breaches and mobile money scams and covering cybersecurity activities in Ghana.
